samples.topic: You would like to spend six months working in head office
samples.q:
You work for an international company, and would like to spend six months working in its head office in another country.

Write a letter to your manager. In your letter:
- explain why you want to work in the company’s head office for six months
- say how your work could be done while you are away
- ask for his/her help in arranging it
samples.sample:
Dear Mr George,

I am writing to express my interest in working at our company headquarters in the United Kingdom for a few months to further enhance my skills and get exposure to the global market trends of our products so that I can better contribute to my company and carry out my responsibilities more efficiently.

As you know, I have been recently promoted to the assistant product manager post and I am working hard to collaborate with my team to enhance the sales and increase our brand reputation. However, I have been feeling the need to meet and work with our global team members and attend some training sessions that our head office in London arranges frequently. I am quite positive that the opportunity to work in our company’s head office for six months will further enhance my knowledge and give me an exposure to the global market trend.

I have talked to Julian and he has agreed to take up my responsibilities during my absence. Furthermore, I will check my emails daily, and be available for emergency phone calls. Once I get back to the office, I would endeavour to work extra hours in order to catch up on anything I had missed.

Finally, I would need your support to get the approvals so that I can work in our company’s head office for six months and fulfil the objectives.

I look forward to your positive reply.

Yours sincerely,

Charles Hugo

samples.topic: Complaints about the reception area where visitors to your company arrive
samples.q:
You work for a company and you are not happy about the reception area where visitors to your company arrive.

Write a letter to your manager. In your letter:
- explain why you are not happy with the current reception area
- say how the arrival of visitors could be improved
- suggest what the manager should do to make these changes
samples.sample:
Dear Mr. Henderson,

I am writing to bring to your attention some concerns regarding our company’s reception area. As you know, the reception is the first point of contact for our visitors, and I believe its current state does not reflect the professional image of our organization.

Currently, the reception area is quite cramped and poorly lit. The seating is outdated and uncomfortable, and there is often a lack of clear signage for visitors. Furthermore, the wait times for visitors to be attended to can be quite long, which I believe creates a negative first impression.

To improve the visitor experience, I suggest we renovate the reception area to make it more spacious and welcoming. This could include upgrading the furniture, improving the lighting, and installing clear digital signage. Additionally, implementing a more efficient visitor management system could help reduce wait times.

I suggest you allocate a budget for these renovations and perhaps form a small committee to oversee the design and implementation of these changes. I would be more than happy to be a part of this committee and contribute my ideas.

I look forward to discussing this further with you.

Yours sincerely,

[Your Name]

samples.topic: A large company in your area has decided to spend a certain amount of money
samples.q:
A large company in your area has decided to spend a certain amount of money on a local facility. You have some ideas on how this money should be spent.

Write a letter to the company manager. In your letter:
- say which local facility you think should be improved
- explain why it needs improvement
- suggest how the money should be spent on this facility
samples.sample:
Dear Manager,

I am writing to express my appreciation for your company's generous decision to invest in our local community. I have some suggestions on how this funding could be most effectively used to benefit the residents of our area.

I believe the local public library would be a prime candidate for improvement. Our library is a vital resource for people of all ages, providing access to books, educational programs, and technology. However, it is currently in need of significant upgrades.

The library’s computer facilities are outdated and often non-functional, which limits the ability of students and job-seekers to access essential online resources. Furthermore, the building itself requires some structural maintenance, particularly the roof and the heating system, which are currently inefficient.

I suggest the funds be used to purchase new, high-specification computers and to upgrade the library’s internet infrastructure. Additionally, a portion of the money could be allocated to repairing the building’s structural issues to ensure a comfortable environment for all users. These improvements would significantly enhance the library's role as a cornerstone of our community.

Thank you for considering my suggestions.

Yours sincerely,

[Your Name]

samples.topic: During a recent plane journey, you sat next to a businessman
samples.q:
During a recent plane journey, you sat next to a businessman who told you about his company. You are now interested in working for this company.

Write a letter to the businessman. In your letter:
- remind him who you are and where you met
- say why you are interested in working for his company
- tell him about your skills and experience
samples.sample:
Dear Mr. Sterling,

I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to follow up on our conversation during our flight from Singapore to London last week. I was the person sitting next to you in seat 14B, and I truly enjoyed our discussion about the current trends in the tech industry.

After hearing about your company, 'InnoTech Solutions,' and its innovative approach to sustainable energy, I have become very interested in the possibility of joining your team. Your description of the company’s mission and the collaborative culture you've built resonated with my own professional values.

As I mentioned briefly during our flight, I have over five years of experience in project management within the renewable energy sector. My skills include strategic planning, team leadership, and a proven track record of delivering complex projects on time and within budget. I believe my background and passion for sustainability would make me a valuable asset to InnoTech Solutions.

I would appreciate the opportunity to talk further about any potential openings in your company. I have attached my CV for your review.

Thank you for your time and for the inspiring conversation.

Yours sincerely,

[Your Name]
